turns.prompt_text: I have used Google Chrome and I have many different tabs open. I combine them into tab groups. I have a window open right now with every tab group selected. I would like to create a Google Sheets with every tab URL or link or address and I would like to have them grouped by their groups. But I just don't want to have them open any more.
turns.response_html:
Since Chrome does not have a native "Export to Sheets" button, the best approach depends on whether you prefer a "no-install" workaround or a dedicated tool.

Here are three different perspectives on how to solve this, ranging from using native features to community-built tools.

Option 1: The Native "Bookmark" Method (Best for Structure)

This method requires no new software and preserves your Tab Groups as folders, which is helpful for organization in Sheets.

  1. Save the Session: Press Ctrl + Shift + D (Windows/Linux) or Cmd + Shift + D (Mac).
  2. Name the Folder: A dialog will pop up asking for a folder name. Name it (e.g., "Session Export [Date]") and save. Note: Chrome will automatically create sub-folders for each of your Tab Groups inside this main folder.
  3. Export to HTML:
    • Go to the Bookmark Manager (Ctrl + Shift + O or Cmd + Shift + B).
    • Click the three dots (top right) $\rightarrow$ Export Bookmarks.
    • Save the HTML file to your computer.
  4. Import to Sheets:
    • Open a new Google Sheet.
    • Use the IMPORTXML function to pull the links from that HTML file, or (easier) open the HTML file in a text editor (like Notepad or VS Code), copy the text, and paste it into Sheets.
    • Tip: Since the export is HTML, you can also just drag the HTML file into a new Chrome tab, copy the list of links it displays, and paste that directly into Sheets.

Option 2: The Extension Method (Best for Speed)

If you are comfortable installing a temporary extension, this is the fastest way to get a clean text list to paste into Sheets.

  • OneTab: This is a popular extension that reduces all open tabs into a single list.
    1. Install OneTab.
    2. Click the OneTab icon. It will instantly close all open tabs and create a single page with a list of links grouped by when they were open.
    3. Click "Export / Import URLs" in the top right of the OneTab page.
    4. Copy the resulting text list and paste it directly into Google Sheets.
  • Copy All Urls: Another lightweight extension specifically for this. It copies all open tab URLs to your clipboard in text or JSON format, which you can paste immediately.

Option 3: The "Copy Link" Feature (Fastest Native Attempt)

If you are on a very recent version of Chrome, you might be able to force a copy without extensions, though it is inconsistent compared to Edge:

  1. Click the first tab in your window.
  2. Hold Shift and click the last tab (this selects all tabs).
  3. Right-click on one of the tabs.
  4. Look for "Copy site links" (Note: This is standard in Microsoft Edge but rolling out/experimental in some Chrome builds). If you see it, click it, and you can paste the full list directly into Sheets.

Next Step

Once you have pasted your links into Sheets, you can safely close that Chrome window. Would you like me to explain how to use a formula in Google Sheets to automatically clean up the URLs (e.g., removing the "https://" or extracting just the domain name)?
